hero.description: Pristine TypeScript types compiled into live runtime blueprints. Zero schema duplication, zero bundle inflation.

blockOne.description: Xalor is an ahead-of-time (AOT) type metadata engine for TypeScript. Instead of forcing you to write complex runtime validation schemas by hand or generating messy boilerplate files that clutter your project, Xalor extracts your native TypeScript definitions during compilation and makes them instantly available at runtime.

blockTwo.description: TypeScript removes type definitions during compilation, leaving production code unable to verify network data. Other tools fix this with duplicate schemas or bloated generated files that slow down code editors. Xalor solves both problems automatically by capturing your types during the standard build pass.
list: _Write native TypeScript once_ —  Eliminate duplicate schemas, manual syncing errors, and custom validation languages.
_Reuse the same types at runtime_ —  Enforce clean structural contracts natively for instant validation, type-guards, and parsing gates.
_Unlock runtime type intelligence_ —  Go beyond validation to power automated data normalization, safe default populating, and legacy schema updates.

one.description: _Write your data models once_ using native, pristine TypeScript. Xalor transforms them into **ironclad runtime contracts** automatically during your `build pass`—completely eliminating duplicate schema authoring or non-native validation languages.

two.description: Heavy `Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)` analysis happens entirely during compilation, never in production. Your application ships only with compact, **content-addressed metadata maps** instead of thousands of lines of heavy validation source code.

three.description: Xalor mines your code's type topology out-of-band during your toolchain's standard compilation window. Enjoy _zero-maintenance syncing freedom_ with **hard-zero local folder pollution**, generated files, or editor save lag.

header.description: A high-performance type engine that reads your native TypeScript definitions to handle automatic, ultra-fast data validation at runtime—with zero code bloat, zero duplicate schemas, and zero background resource waste.

singleSourceOfTruth.description: Every other validation framework forces you into a _double-maintenance tax_. You have to manually write custom runtime validation schema language blocks (like a Zod schema) and then write a mirrored TypeScript interface right next to it just to get basic editor autocompletion.
singleSourceOfTruth.subDescription: Xalor treats your standard, everyday TypeScript types as the absolute, **single source of truth**. You write a standard type, pass its token to Xalor's execution perimeters, and the engine takes over. If you modify or delete a type property, your workspace data layers adapt instantly with **hard-zero duplication overhead**.

image.alt: Xalor Pipeline Overview: Eradicating the Dual-Source Schema Tax

codeBlock.note: Study the programmatic lifecycle flow in the diagram. When you save a type declaration (`Step I`), our background watcher intercepts the pass. The **Ghost Emitter** (`Step II`) deploys an `Atomic Shield` to stream your layout keys safely to autocomplete maps, while the engine triggers an in-memory **Vault Compaction** pass (`Step III`). When raw production data hits your `Boundary Gate` (`Step IV`), lookups run at bare-metal velocity via hard $O(1)$ pointer assignments.

aotPipeline.description: Xalor permanently eliminates runtime type erasure by mining your code's type topology *before compilation erasure* takes place. The engine hooks directly into the native TypeScript Compiler API pass, routing nodes point-free through a cascade of specialized, self-cleaning type-predicate reifiers.
aotPipeline.subDescription: This functional extraction loop guarantees **absolute zero structural mutation** or unsafe type-casting (`as any`). It evaluates your code's raw geometric layout entirely inside an isolated, volatile in-memory scratchpad, preparing the types to be serialized into invariant blueprints with zero folder pollution.

codeBlock.code:
[ AST Node Pass ] ──► Analyzed by theMiner loop
        │
        ▼
[ Pre-Reification Gates ] ──► Lineage verification via Symbol IDs
        │
        ▼
[ Deep Shape Unroller ] ──► Extracted into un-normalized TSolidShape
        │
        ▼
[ Canonical Serialization ] ──► Flattened by serializeCanonicalFingerprint
        │
        ▼
[ Content-Addressable Pool ] ──► Deduplicated into invariant sh_ entries
codeBlock.note: All type registrations enter through a unified funnel (`transformer/index.ts`). Each evaluation path receives an isolated tracking frame, preserving purity, recursion safety, and deterministic compilation.

casFingerprinting.description: Standard compiler macros duplicate checking structures repeatedly across your application source files. Xalor implements an immutable, zero-dependency **Content-Addressable Storage (CAS)** system driven by a stable bitwise `FNV-1a` hashing engine that treats structural signatures exactly like a Git repository committing code changes.
casFingerprinting.subDescription: By passing reified nodes into `serializeCanonicalFingerprint()`, the engine runs an allocation-free flattening sweep that strips nominal data to isolate absolute geometric layouts. Properties are sorted alphabetically, circular stacks are defused via a transient `visited` cache frame, and the resulting invariant DNA string is compressed into an **8-character footprint** prefixed with `sh_`.

codeBlock.note: Look at the compaction ratio. If an interface pattern (like `Address` or `UserMetadata`) is referenced across 500 separate endpoints, it is compiled and loaded into your RAM exactly once inside `blueprints["sh_4vztgu"]`. The other 500 parent records simply store a tiny reference string pointer token, completely flattening your application's overall memory footprint budget curve.

phantomBuild.description: Traditional validation frameworks force production systems to ingest, compile, and execute thousands of lines of heavy, nested JavaScript schema code. As your application models scale from **10 to 500** complex definitions, your client-facing build scripts bloat with un-tree-shakable validation logic that directly degrades your _Google Lighthouse scores_.
phantomBuild.subDescription: Xalor eliminates this performance degradation through an automated **Parallel Production Split**. Our ahead-of-time (AOT) toolchain watcher strips away all development type telemetry from your client-side application scripts, moving the raw type configurations into a decoupled, server-side `CAS blueprint vault`.

codeBlock.note: Repeated structures collapse into shared blueprint references during the `AOT Compaction Sweep`. Nested shapes are stored once and resolved through lightweight pointers, enabling deterministic **O(1) hydration** at runtime.

typeGraphTelemetry.description: Validation is merely a beneficial runtime side-effect. By extracting deep, structural compile-time metadata blueprints, Xalor answers the ultimate engineering question: `What else can you do with types?` It transforms your static contracts into an active infrastructure layer that powers automated mock simulation, live graph tracing, and cross-era schema transformations.
typeGraphTelemetry.subDescription: While our local orchestration web dashboard is finalizing, invoking `npx xalor studio` forces the background compiler toolchain to map out your application's complete structural schema network. The background watcher flattens your codebase dependencies into an **isomorphic shared edge topology matrix**, ready to be visualized as live 3D relationship lineages or piped natively into runtime strategy engines.

#Because your codebase geometry is pre-compiled into an optimized key-value mapping, your types unlock an extensible runtime intelligence layer.

 Pass your reference keys into our 6 core strategy vectors:#

​

`xalor.parse()` #— Executes high-velocity structural verification and returns nominally-branded variables.#

​

`xalor.guard()` #— Provides an assertive inline type-guard function for safely passing unknown objects.#

​

​

​

`xalor.clone()` #— Performs circular-safe object duplication while preserving internal structural identity.#

contentList.description: Generates a stateless **type predicate closure** for sub-microsecond payload narrowing at runtime boundaries.
Isolates execution side-effects, returning a clean result block containing a boolean flag and a flat **collected validation error list**.
Synchronously evaluates incoming shapes against blueprints, throwing **traceable GPS diagnostics** on failure.
Manufactures **safe fallback structures** pre-hydrated with system primitives to prevent undefined crashes.

Performs a **deep, circular-safe copy** of an input object while completely scrubbing away lingering keys, unmapped attributes, or trailing closure noise not explicitly permitted by the type contract.
Fuses schemas symmetrically; matching primitives overwrite, nested objects fuse, and arrays combine **item-by-item**.
Executes a **10-phase upcast pipeline** to safely migrate historical backend payloads into current production layouts on the fly.
Combines multiple **independent registry contracts** into a unified validation execution graph.
Forces loose external payload structures into compliance by safely mapping mismatched **primitive variants**.
Generates randomized, high-entropy fixtures natively from blueprints, unlocking **strongly-typed Simulacrum property overrides**.
Computes a flat **structural delta matrix** contrasting property discrepancies across two active shapes.

statusList.name: xalor compile
statusList.description: Executes a manual, out-of-band workspace AST sweep to discover schemas, map relational structures, and compile type snapshots down to the cache directory.

statusList.name: xalor vacuum
statusList.description: Triggers the production gatekeeper phase: synchronizes memory graphs, executes absolute client shedding to amputate telemetry, and delivers the minified json bytecode contract.

statusList.name: xalor audit
statusList.description: Profiles internal metadata compaction metrics, inspects Content-Addressable Storage deduplication ratios, and scans call-sites for dead-code orphans.

statusList.name: xalor studio
statusList.description: Launches the local interactive playground dashboard to visualize contract lineage evolution and test polymorphic pattern matching layers via a local browser port.

statusList.name: xalor clear
statusList.description: Flushes all localized environment data stores, unlinks temporary background file buffers, and resets the project envelope to a pristine, uncompiled baseline state.

statusList.name: xalor help
statusList.description: Outputs full system syntax layout parameters, available configuration flags, and explicit execution commands directly to the terminal.

simulacrumGeneratorUtils.name: uuid
simulacrumGeneratorUtils.description: Generates a standards-compliant UUID v4 string suitable for unique identifiers, database keys, request tracing, and distributed systems. Each invocation produces a new 36-character RFC 4122 UUID.

simulacrumGeneratorUtils.name: compactId
simulacrumGeneratorUtils.description: Generates a cryptographically secure, URL-safe identifier optimized for database keys, routing segments, cache keys, and temporary identifiers. The generated value contains only Base64URL-safe characters and defaults to 10 characters in length.

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Optional. Specifies the desired length of the generated identifier. Values are clamped between 4 and 128 characters. Defaults to 10.

simulacrumGeneratorUtils.name: percentage
simulacrumGeneratorUtils.description: Generates a realistic percentage value using configurable statistical bias distributions. Useful for producing believable completion rates, confidence scores, utilization metrics, and other percentage-based mock data.

parameters.name: bias
parameters.description: Optional. Determines how values are distributed. 'flat' generates values evenly across the full range, 'low' favors lower percentages, and 'high' favors higher percentages. Defaults to 'flat'.

parameters.name: decimals
parameters.description: Optional. Specifies the number of decimal places to include. Values are clamped between 0 and 4. Defaults to 2.

simulacrumGeneratorUtils.name: currency
simulacrumGeneratorUtils.description: Generates a realistic, localized currency amount formatted using the runtime's native Intl.NumberFormat API. Supports configurable value ranges, locales, and ISO 4217 currency codes.

parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Specifies the minimum value that can be generated.

parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Specifies the maximum value that can be generated.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: A valid BCP 47 locale used to format the generated value (for example, 'en-US', 'de-DE', or 'ja-JP').

parameters.name: currency
parameters.description: A valid ISO 4217 currency code used when formatting the generated amount (for example, 'USD', 'EUR', or 'JPY').

simulacrumGeneratorUtils.name: email
simulacrumGeneratorUtils.description: Generates a realistic, pronounceable email address derived from a property name. The same property key will always produce the same email address, making it ideal for deterministic mock data generation.

parameters.name: propertyKey
parameters.description: The property name used as the deterministic seed when generating the email address. Different property names produce different, but repeatable, email addresses.

simulacrumGeneratorUtils.name: userHandle
simulacrumGeneratorUtils.description: Generates a realistic, human-readable user handle derived from a property name. The same property key will always produce the same handle, making it ideal for deterministic usernames, display names, and mock profile data.

parameters.name: propertyKey
parameters.description: The property name used as the deterministic seed when generating the user handle. Different property names produce different, but repeatable, handles.

simulacrumGeneratorUtils.name: loremIpsum
simulacrumGeneratorUtils.description: Generates realistic placeholder text as plain text or Markdown. Configure the number of paragraphs, sentences, and words to produce anything from a single sentence to a multi-section Markdown document.

parameters.name: paragraphs
parameters.description: The number of paragraphs to generate. Values are clamped between 1 and 16.

parameters.name: sentencesPerParagraph
parameters.description: The number of sentences to generate per paragraph. A value of 0 produces a randomized sentence count for each paragraph. Values are clamped between 0 and 16.

parameters.name: wordsPerSentence
parameters.description: The number of words to generate per sentence. A value of 0 produces a randomized word count for each sentence. Values are clamped between 0 and 32.

parameters.name: includeHeader
parameters.description: Determines whether Markdown formatting, including headings, quotes, and list elements, is included in the generated output.

simulacrumGeneratorUtils.name: timestamp
simulacrumGeneratorUtils.description: Generates a realistic ISO 8601 timestamp relative to the current runtime moment. Supports configurable past or future offsets using compact relative time patterns with optional natural drift to simulate real-world event timing.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Optional. Defines the relative offset from the current timestamp using a compact pattern format. The first character specifies direction ('+' for future timestamps, '-' for past timestamps), the numeric portion specifies the amount, and the final character specifies the unit. Supported units include seconds (s), minutes (m), hours (h), days (d), and other configured time units. Defaults to '-0m'.

parameters.name: allowDrift
parameters.description: Optional. Adds a natural ±10% timing variation to the calculated offset to produce more realistic simulated event timestamps. When disabled, the timestamp is generated at the exact requested offset. Defaults to true.

simulacrumGeneratorUtils.name: mockJwt
simulacrumGeneratorUtils.description: Generates a structurally valid mock JSON Web Token (JWT) string for authentication flows, testing environments, and simulated authorization scenarios. Produces a deterministic three-part Base64URL token format containing a header, payload, and signature segment without performing cryptographic signing.

simulacrumGeneratorUtils.name: maskedString
simulacrumGeneratorUtils.description: Generates an anonymized version of a string by masking sensitive characters according to a selected redaction strategy. Useful for simulating privacy-safe logs, GDPR-style data scrubbing, credential protection, and partially hidden identifiers such as emails or payment references.

parameters.name: sourceValue
parameters.description: The source string value to anonymize. The generator preserves the original string structure while replacing selected characters with the configured mask character.

parameters.name: strategy
parameters.description: Optional. Determines the masking behavior. 'full' replaces every character, 'creditCard' preserves the first and last four characters while masking the middle section, and 'email' preserves the first email character, separators, and domain structure while hiding identifying portions. Defaults to 'full'.

parameters.name: maskChar
parameters.description: Optional. Defines the character used for redaction. '*' produces standard privacy masking, while 'X' produces an alternate replacement style. Defaults to '*'.

simulacrumGeneratorUtils.name: miniBlockCipher
simulacrumGeneratorUtils.description:
Generates a lightweight reversible Feistel-style block transformation for structural string obfuscation and simulated cipher workflows.

This utility is designed as a compact mini cipher handler for testing, deterministic masking, and token transformation scenarios. It provides encryption and reification modes using a small configurable round-based Feistel network rather than production-grade cryptographic primitives.

Inspired by the low-level byte manipulation patterns explored in ByteBits: https://github.com/bgskinner3/ByteBits

parameters.name: plaintext
parameters.description: The input string to transform. In 'encrypt' mode this represents the raw payload. In 'decrypt' mode this should be the generated 16-character hexadecimal cipher block.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Optional. Defines the deterministic seed used to generate the internal Feistel round keys. Different keys produce different reversible transformations. Defaults to 1337.

parameters.name: rounds
parameters.description: Optional. Controls the number of Feistel transformation rounds. Values are clamped between 2 and 16 to maintain predictable execution cost. Defaults to 4.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Optional. Selects the transformation direction. 'encrypt' converts plaintext into a fixed hexadecimal block representation, while 'decrypt' reverses a previously generated block representation. Defaults to 'encrypt'.
